Claims that Waze collects sensitive government information or lets others exploit user data are completely false, the company says.
SINGAPORE: Navigation app Waze on Thursday (Oct 22) rejected allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows users' personal data to be exploited, a day after Malaysia banned civil servants from using the app and urged Malaysians to uninstall it.
The company said in a statement to Reuters that claims it collected sensitive government information or allowed any entity to exploit personal data were completely false.
"Waze operates under strict privacy policies that protect user data and comply with global legal data protection standards," a company spokesperson said.
The response came after Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim ordered an immediate ban on the use of Waze by civil servants, citing concerns about the security of government information and personal data.
The Prime Minister's Office said in a statement on Wednesday that the ban was intended "to protect government information and users' personal data from the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime".
Anwar had said the government was looking into potential security risks arising from the use of Waze, which he said was subject to Israeli laws.
He recommended TuJu, a Malaysian navigation app developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative.
Launched in November 2025, Tuju has a live traffic information feature that allows users to view CCTV feeds of selected highway locations, letting them check traffic visually before or during their journeys.
Users can also check toll fares and facilities at rest stops along highways for better route planning during longer journeys.
TuJu also allows users to report road damage and infrastructure problems, while an SOS button lets users seek emergency assistance.
The app has had 700,000 downloads to date, Bernama reported.
"Version 2.0 has been launched for Android users, while its release for iOS is expected by the end of this month, pending the completion of testing on the Apple App Store,” Bernama reported Malaysian Highway Authority Operations and Maintenance director Mohd Shahrir Amin Ahmad as saying.
Bernama also reported on Thursday that TuJu experienced a technical disruption after a significant increase in users following Anwar's comments for Malaysians to switch to Tuju.
"Improvements will continue to ensure that TuJu provides a more stable, accurate and user-friendly service," the Malaysian Highway Authority was reported as saying in a statement.
Malaysia, a staunch supporter of the Palestinian cause, does not maintain diplomatic relations with Israel.
National Security Council director-general Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin told the Malaysian parliament on Thursday that Waze’s new terms of use was a factor in the government’s decision to ban the app’s use by civil servants.
"The new terms of use state that the use of Waze is subject to Israeli law, which was not the case previously. As a result, any legal disputes would be subject to Israeli law, even though Malaysia does not recognise that country,” he said, as reported in Bernama.
"I want to stress that this decision is not solely about technology, but also concerns the laws governing users' data."
Raja Nushirwan added that the Malaysian government would not compromise on the country’s information sovereignty, stressing that Malaysian data cannot be subject to Israeli jurisdiction.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said that Waze’s terms of service falling under Israeli legal jurisdiction raises concerns over movement data security and potential difficulties in seeking legal recourse.
Gobind added that the Waze ban does not apply to general members of the public using the app for personal purposes, and that civil servants were not restricted to using the TuJu app, and could continue using alternatives, including Google Maps, for official duties.
Waze was founded in Israel and uses satellite signals and information supplied by drivers to provide real-time traffic updates.
Google, which is owned by Alphabet, acquired the navigation app in 2013.

On the morning of October 22nd, continuing the program of the 2nd Session, Minister of Justice Hoang Thanh Tung presented the report on the draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended).
Amendments and additions to regulations on real estate business contracts.
According to the Minister of Justice, the draft law consists of 10 chapters and 61 articles, with some new additions: regardingReal estate transaction procedures, which stipulate the principles for conducting transactions and the framework for real estate transaction processes.

Expand the types of transfer contracts in real estate business.
The draft law also includes many provisions to address difficulties and obstacles in practice, ensuring consistency with related laws; promoting digital transformation ; and regulating matters of a principled and framework nature.
This includes amending and supplementing the general provisions of the Law on Real Estate Business, such asClarify the scope of regulation, excluding the subjects, transaction procedures, and contracts for the purchase, lease, or lease-purchase of social housing and policy-based housing; fully regulate the public disclosure of information on projects put into business, the timing of disclosure, and the responsibility of businesses to update; amend regulations stipulating that foreign organizations and individuals, and people of Vietnamese origin residing abroad, are only allowed to purchase housing and types of construction works not associated with the transfer of land use rights.

Amendments and additions to regulations on real estate business contracts. Specifically,完善 the system of contract types, ensuring full compliance with form and content requirements, and suitability for the types of real estate actually traded.
Clarify the principles, governing bodies, conditions, and procedures for applying contracts; standardize the application of contracts according to the Law on Real Estate Business, resolving overlaps with laws on consumer protection, especially regulations on registration of standard contracts for the purchase and sale of apartment units.
The regulations are being amended to include provisions for real estate business contracts established and transacted electronically, aiming to promote the application of information technology and digital transformation in the real estate business.
Regarding the registration of apartment purchase and sale contracts, the Government has directed relevant agencies to review and agree on a solution aimed at eliminating the registration procedure for apartment purchase and sale contracts.
Accordingly, the draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended) has added a provision that contracts for the purchase and sale of apartment units must be publicly disclosed on the Housing and Real Estate Market Information System before being applied, and are not required to undergo registration and public disclosure procedures as stipulated by other laws.
Please distinguish between deposit agreements and fundraising.
Reviewing the draft law, Chairman of the Economic and Finance Committee Phan Van Mai stated that regarding the right to purchase or lease-purchase real estate by entities with foreign elements, the committee requested clarification on the necessity of expanding the scope of real estate that foreign organizations and individuals are allowed to purchase or lease-purchase, a thorough and comprehensive assessment of the impact on the socio-economic and business investment environment, and ensuring that the institutional framework is correct and fully in line with the spirit of Resolution No. 21-NQ/TW.
Simultaneously, clarify the scope of rights of each entity; registration and transfer conditions; boundaries of owned property, common use areas, access and exploitation rights for structures with multiple layers of usable space; scope, boundaries, location, criteria, and characteristics of accessible areas; and clarify mechanisms for truly strict and effective management, monitoring, and control to ensure national defense, security, order, and social safety.
You may also like
Clarify the mechanism for issuing Certificates of Ownership for houses, construction works, and floor area within construction works in cases not associated with land use rights, the conditions for implementation, and the mechanism for handling transfers, in order to have specific regulations in the draft amended Land Law.
Regarding the business of real estate under construction, the committee proposed that the law stipulate the principles for managing the remaining funds equivalent to 5% of the contract value in the account and handling arising risks; clarifying the element of "voluntariness" when the buyer or leaseholder independently applies for a Certificate of Ownership.
Some have suggested distinguishing between deposit agreements and fundraising for project implementation; and establishing regulations to control other sources of revenue that are essentially fundraising activities prior to the permitted time...
Regarding real estate business contracts, the committee recommends further thorough research on revising the concept of "real estate business" and expanding the types of contracts that can be transferred; if the practical basis, transaction needs, specific issues to be resolved, and added value of the policy are not yet clarified, and the impact and risk control mechanisms have not been fully assessed, it is recommended that these provisions not be included in the draft law.
In addition, it is suggested that the relationship between publicizing standard contract forms and registering standard contract forms be clarified. A review and clear regulation should be established specifying cases where notarization or certification is mandatory, while other cases allow for selection based on the requirements of the parties involved in the transaction.

articles.summary: Boosting the 'locomotive' of the Southeast region.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
This was also an urgent requirement raised at the conference "Banking sector accompanying and unlocking financial and banking resources to serve growth in the Southeast region" on the afternoon of October 23, as the economy enters the "final sprint" of 2026.
 Capital is to the economy like water to a field: wherever it flows, vitality flourishes. The Southeast region, encompassing Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai City, and Tay Ninh province, is the most dynamic economic region in the country, accounting for approximately 31.4% of GDP and attracting about 42% of registered FDI capital in the first nine months of 2026. As the largest driver of national growth, the region needs investment capital commensurate with its potential and development requirements.
 In Ho Chi Minh City, the GRDP for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 9.06%, the highest for the same period in a decade; FDI reached US$17.8 billion, 4.2 times higher than the same period. However, a major challenge lies ahead: in the fourth quarter, the GRDP must increase by 13.23% to reach 10.2% for the whole year. During the 2026-2030 period, the city needs over VND 1 trillion in social investment capital each year.
 It is concerning that capital flows are not uniform, while the capacity to absorb capital varies significantly across economic sectors. Credit increased by 18.64%, budget capital increased by 25.8%, but private sector and household capital only increased by 5.3%. Credit to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) increased by 6.7%, while the number of dissolved businesses increased 2.7 times.
 Many projects and land plots remain stalled due to legal obstacles, financial obligations, and collateral issues. The challenge, therefore, is not just about how much more capital can be mobilized, but also about removing the barriers that hinder capital from reaching businesses and projects; and improving the ability to absorb and utilize resources effectively.
 Unlocking capital flows primarily means removing obstacles to accessing credit and directing resources towards sectors and projects that have the potential to boost growth.
 For large-scale projects such as urban railways and inter-regional expressways, it is necessary to study appropriate long-term financing mechanisms, promote syndicated loan models, and meet investment needs while ensuring the safety of the banking system.
 With high technology, a green economy, and innovative startups, banks need to boldly expand lending based on cash flow, contracts, and intellectual property assets as regulated. In the fourth quarter alone, supporting interest rate reductions for production and exports, restructuring debt appropriately, and expanding credit for social housing... will be timely solutions to provide support.
 At the same time, it is necessary to accelerate the buying and selling of debts, resolve legal obstacles, and release collateral assets when conditions are met in order to "unfreeze" stalled projects, and return land and capital to serve the economy.
 But a great river cannot have only one source. Bank credit alone cannot bear the burden of projects that last for decades. Local government bonds, green bonds, project bonds, the stock market, and investment funds need to become additional capital raising channels to meet medium- and long-term capital needs and stimulate private investment.
 In that picture, the Vietnam International Finance Center in Ho Chi Minh City is expected to become a "gateway" welcoming global capital flows. Financial products are linked to the region's infrastructure project portfolio; a controlled pilot mechanism, along with an effective monitoring and dispute resolution system, will ensure that this "gateway" truly facilitates trade.
 Every river needs a solid riverbed. This is achieved through a transparent institutional framework, from the implementation of the Urban Development Law and the completion of the Ho Chi Minh City Master Plan for the period 2025-2050, with a 100-year vision, to resolving land-related issues and site clearance. It also involves regional linkages, with three localities jointly developing a list of projects and sharing data to enable banks to quickly and accurately assess and disburse funds according to needs.
 When the government plays a proactive role, banks actively cooperate, and businesses are determined to invest, bottlenecks in mobilizing and utilizing capital will be gradually removed, creating a strong flow of resources for development.
 That is the driving force for the Southeast region to maintain its leading role, creating a ripple effect and accelerating the national economy in the 2026-2030 period.

articles.summary: Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam: Interest rate reduction should be focused and targeted.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Reduce lending interest rates by 1.5% to 2% for priority sectors.
 Speaking at the conference "Banking Sector Accompanying and Unlocking Financial and Banking Resources to Serve Growth in the Southeast Region in the Period 2026 - 2030," held on the afternoon of October 23, Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) Pham Duc An stated that the SBV's operational work must pursue multiple objectives, contributing to macroeconomic stability, controlling inflation, ensuring the safety of the banking system, and supporting economic growth.
 The State Bank of Vietnam has specified objectives and solutions for the entire system regarding monetary policy, credit, restructuring, handling bad debts, inspection and supervision, administrative procedure reform, promoting cashless payments, digital transformation of banking operations, and ensuring the security and safety of payment operations.
 In particular, regarding credit operations, to facilitate credit institutions, at the end of 2025, the State Bank of Vietnam announced and immediately assigned credit growth targets for 2026 so that credit institutions could proactively meet the capital needs of people, businesses, and the economy.
 At the same time, the State Bank of Vietnam has directed credit institutions to resolutely implement solutions to achieve the right and targeted credit growth from the beginning of the year, strengthen the review and simplification of credit granting processes and procedures, optimize the application of digital transformation in credit granting processes, create favorable conditions for accessing bank credit, stabilize deposit interest rates, contribute to stabilizing the monetary market, and contribute to striving to reduce lending interest rates…
 Interest rate and exchange rate management is linked to international developments. The State Bank of Vietnam closely monitors the situation to manage interest rates appropriately according to actual conditions and closely follow international developments. According to the Governor, this close monitoring aims to ensure flexible management, maintain macroeconomic stability, and control the exchange rate. 
|  | 
| Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, Pham Duc An  | 
 Maintaining macroeconomic stability, controlling inflation, and stabilizing the value of the Vietnamese Dong are crucial. The relatively stable exchange rate of the Vietnamese Dong, without significant depreciation against other currencies, helps to strengthen the confidence of both the people and foreign investors. This stability contributes to maintaining tens of billions of USD in foreign investment already implemented in Vietnam. If the currency depreciates, mobilizing domestic capital as well as attracting foreign investment will become extremely difficult.
 Continuing to coordinate monetary and fiscal policies in a fundamental and effective manner aims to support inflation control, stabilize exchange rates, and contribute to economic growth. Over the first nine months of the year, the consumer price index (CPI) stood at 4.52%, demonstrating positive results in inflation control thanks to close coordination between monetary and fiscal policies, ministries, and local authorities.
 According to the Governor, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) is focusing on closely directing efforts to minimize unfair competition in capital mobilization among commercial banks. Although major central banks around the world (such as the Fed and ECB) are continuously tightening monetary policy and raising interest rates, the SBV is proactively assessing macroeconomic stability, exchange rates, and ensuring positive real interest rates for depositors.
 The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has directed credit institutions to reduce lending interest rates by 1.5% to 2%, focusing on production and business sectors and priority areas, while also directing a reduction of approximately 0.5% in savings interest rates. This interest rate reduction is being implemented in a targeted and focused manner, rather than a widespread and indiscriminate reduction, ensuring it aligns with current realities without contradicting the global context.
 The Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam also emphasized that credit institutions must step up capital mobilization from the economy to meet credit demand, but strictly prohibits unfair competition, cross-mobilization, or poaching customers from each other among credit institutions.
 Credit orientation and capital risk management for real estate.
 The State Bank of Vietnam has issued very detailed directives (such as documents 98 and 9608), prioritizing system safety and providing financial support for production and business activities. At the same time, it has promptly addressed behaviors that pose risks at credit institutions.
 Each credit institution needs to effectively manage risks to ensure its own safety, thereby contributing to the safety of the entire system and making a positive contribution to the economy. The State Bank of Vietnam, together with credit institutions, will research specific solutions to remove legal obstacles, especially those related to tangible assets, intangible assets, innovation, and intellectual property.
 Credit flows must be focused on priority production and business sectors of the economy, in line with established policies. Programs and credit product packages should be developed to suit each market segment. However, recognizing market feedback regarding high lending interest rates in some areas, the State Bank of Vietnam will continue to direct credit institutions to reduce lending interest rates for production and business sectors.
 Implement synchronized solutions to strengthen payment connectivity and the connection between banks and businesses, under the direction of local Party committees and authorities. Communication efforts by the State Bank of Vietnam and credit institutions play a particularly important role in helping the public and society understand, agree with, support, and cooperate effectively with the activities of the banking sector.
 However, the Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam believes that businesses need to enhance their proactiveness, diversify their capital sources, innovate in the market, and effectively combine bank credit with other legitimate capital sources to proactively develop business plans.
 In recent times, the real estate market has developed strongly, and bank credit has contributed a significant amount to this sector. Strictly implementing the Prime Minister 's directive on tightly controlling the market, preventing speculation, manipulation, and price gouging of real estate is crucial.
 The banking sector and businesses must define new strategies for this new phase; they cannot continue to push up real estate prices to create an artificial market. In reality, unbalanced real estate growth will have significant negative consequences for overall economic growth.
 Real estate businesses and credit institutions need to restructure their operations; they cannot rely on real estate as a sector that generates super profits. In other words, they must balance the interests of all parties, ensuring sustainable development in the new circumstances. The banking sector will continue to play an important role, but will manage risks and operate under a more cautious new mechanism.
 The banking sector hopes that local Party committees and authorities (in the two cities and provinces of the Southeast region) will actively support the removal of obstacles related to mechanisms, land procedures, planning, and infrastructure for projects. Once the authorities remove procedural obstacles, allowing projects to commence construction and investment sooner, this will be a prerequisite for businesses to improve their ability to absorb capital and repay bank loans.

JAKARTA, – Malaysian offshore geotechnical specialist Helms Geomarine Sdn Bhd (HELMS) has signed a memorandum of understanding with PT Elnusa Trans Samudera (ENTS) to pursue offshore drilling and seabed investigation contracts in Indonesia and Timor-Leste, with plans to develop local vessel and technical capabilities.
The agreement, signed on October 21 by Dato’ Ir. Helmi Zulkawi, Managing Director of HELMS, and Kurniawati Adjie, Director of ENTS, combines specialist drilling equipment and expertise with Indonesian marine operations and logistics support.
Partnership targets offshore energy projects
The companies intend to pursue offshore geotechnical investigations involving drilling, soil and rock sampling, seabed testing, laboratory analysis and engineering reports.
Such investigations provide essential information for offshore energy developments, helping engineers assess seabed conditions before installing foundations, pipelines and other infrastructure.
HELMS brings experience from offshore oil and gas projects across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Australia, alongside offshore wind developments in Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.
The Malaysian company maintains long-term contracts with energy operators including PETRONAS, Shell and PTTEP.
ENTS, a subsidiary of ELNUSA within the Pertamina Hulu Energi Group, will contribute marine services, local operational knowledge and logistical support.
DP2 vessels support regional expansion
HELMS currently operates two dynamically positioned geotechnical vessels, Keyfield Helms 1 and Keyfield Itqan.
Both vessels provide a platform for offshore investigation activities where accurate positioning is important during drilling and seabed sampling operations.
The company’s management team also has experience working in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea dating back to the 1990s. HELMS considers the geological and operating conditions in those markets comparable to those encountered in Timor-Leste.
Local investment and technical training planned
Beyond pursuing individual contracts, the partnership envisages establishing a local HELMS entity to hold strategic drilling resources and support longer-term operations.
The proposed arrangements include deploying Indonesian-flagged DP2 vessels, employing Indonesian personnel and developing local laboratory testing facilities.
Technical training and knowledge sharing are also planned to build domestic capabilities in offshore geotechnical investigation.
The agreement remains a framework for cooperation, with specific project awards, investment commitments and implementation schedules yet to be announced.
The companies also intend to coordinate vessel preparation and mobilisation, laboratory services and engineering support as they pursue offshore investigation opportunities in both markets.

articles.title: Women entrepreneurs who have helped shape Vietnam’s 40 years of reform - Theinvestor
articles.summary: Women entrepreneurs who have helped shape Vietnam’s 40 years of reform  Theinvestor
articles.full_text:
The 40-year journey of economic reform (Doi moi) bears the mark of significant contributions from the private sector, particularly pioneering women entrepreneurs. From economic opening to global integration, they have built businesses and driven new growth.
In 1986, when Vietnam embarked on its Doi moi, the private sector was still in its infancy. The stock market had yet to be established, state-owned enterprises dominated the economy, and Vietnamese companies investing and operating across borders remained a distant prospect.
Four decades later, the landscape has changed dramatically. Vietnam is now home to large private domestic enterprises, brands competing in international markets, conglomerates investing in aviation, banking, energy and high-tech agriculture, and exporters increasingly integrated into global value chains.
The journeys of several women entrepreneurs reflect this transformation across successive stages: from businesses established during the early years of economic opening to equitization, the emergence of capital markets and, ultimately, expansion into industries requiring ever greater capital, technology and management expertise.
From early market opening to major investment deals
One of the most significant changes brought about by Doi moi was the emergence and growth of the private sector. Many businesses began in trading, manufacturing or services before gradually expanding their scale and operations.
Nguyen Thi Nga is one such example. She built BRG from its beginnings in import-export trading in 1993. As the group grew, her influence became evident not only in its expansion but also in mergers and acquisitions (M&A) involving assets with strategic locations and development potential.
In 1999, BRG acquired a golf course in Dong Mo, Hanoi from a foreign investor, at a time when golf was still a nascent market in Vietnam and players were predominantly international visitors.
Following the acquisition, the company gradually upgraded the Lakeside course, developed MountainView and Kings Course, and partnered with international companies on golf course design and operations.
From Dong Mo, BRG expanded into other golf projects, including Legend Hill, Legend Danang Golf Resort, Legend Valley Country Club and projects in Hue city, central Vietnam. Golf gradually became part of a broader service offering that connected accommodation, dining, leisure and experiential activities.
After entering the golf sector, BRG expanded into hospitality, partnering with international hotel operators and brands such as Hilton, Marriott International and IHG. Its projects included Hilton Garden Inn Hanoi and Sheraton Grand Danang Resort, as well as plans to rebrand Hilton Hanoi Opera under the Waldorf Astoria brand.
What stands out about these deals is that the M&A strategy went beyond changing asset ownership. After acquiring the properties, BRG continued investing in upgrades, reshaping its offerings, introducing international operating standards, and integrating the assets with other businesses across its ecosystem.
From standalone golf courses and hotels, the group gradually developed an integrated model spanning accommodation, leisure, golf, dining and experiential services.
BRG’s story illustrates a broader shift among Vietnamese private enterprises after Doi moi: from trading and capital accumulation to large-scale investments, partnerships with international corporations and the development of assets across longer value chains.
On September 12, 2026, Nga was conferred the title of Labor Hero for her contributions during the Doi moi era.
From state-owned enterprise to public company
Doi moi not only created opportunities for new private businesses but also transformed the way many enterprises originally established in the state sector operated.
Mai Kieu Lien is one of the women entrepreneurs who has witnessed nearly the entire course of this transition.
She joined the predecessor of Vinamilk in 1976, when Vietnam’s economy was still centrally planned. She became deputy general director in 1984 and took over as general director in late 1992.
Over the following three decades, Vinamilk underwent major changes. The company was equitized in 2003, listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange in 2006, expanded its production capacity, built its brand, and invested overseas.
Lien’s career has been closely linked to a broader transformation of Vietnamese businesses after Doi moi: the shift from production under a centrally planned system to operating in a competitive market, raising capital through financial markets and seeking opportunities beyond Vietnam’s borders.
In 2005, she was conferred the title of Labor Hero for her contributions during the Doi moi era.
Private enterprises enter bigger leagues
Two decades after Doi moi began, the question facing the private sector was no longer simply whether businesses had the right to operate. A new generation of companies was entering industries requiring larger investments, more advanced technology and stronger management capabilities.
Thai Huong, founder and chairwoman of the strategic council of TH Group, is among the business leaders associated with this trend.
In 2008, she launched a high-tech dairy farming and milk processing project in Nghe An province. TH Group was established a year later.
The project’s significance extended beyond its dairy products. TH’s model demonstrated how private enterprises were beginning to invest heavily in agriculture, apply technology, and organize production across an integrated value chain, from raw materials and farms to processing and distribution.
In 2020, Huong was conferred the title of Labor Hero for her contributions during the Doi moi era.
In another sector, Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao has been associated with the rise of private enterprise in aviation.
She was among the founders of Vietjet, serving as the airline’s vice chairwoman and CEO from 2007 before becoming chairwoman in 2023. She is also standing vice chairwoman of HDBank’s board of directors and chairwoman of Sovico.
Vietjet’s emergence illustrates how significantly the scope of Vietnamese private enterprises has expanded since the early years of Doi moi. Aviation requires substantial capital, sophisticated management, advanced technology and international connectivity.
The establishment of a privately owned airline and its expansion of domestic and international routes demonstrate that the private sector has moved into industries with increasingly demanding investment and operational requirements.
On December 27, 2025, Thao was awarded the title of Labor Hero for her contributions during the Doi moi era.

The British government has been accused of softening its stance towards Myanmar’s military-run government by hosting junta representatives.
Human rights campaigners for Myanmar have said the Andy Burnham government has made a “significant shift in approach” after two ministers hosted a junta representative at official meetings in London.
Burma Campaign UK, a London-based human rights organisation, said the UK is “quietly” normalising relations with the sanctioned military-run regime which is trying to seek legitimacy on the global stage after the 2021 military coup.
The details of the meetings had been made public by the junta rather than the British government departments involved, it said.
Myanmar’s general-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing has been on a diplomatic drive, stepping up engagement with world leaders after facing nearly five years of isolation and sanctions following the 2021 military coup.
Min Aung Hlaing led the military seizure of power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi, plunging the country into a civil war that has killed thousands of people, according to rights groups.
On 14 October, the foreign office reportedly hosted Win Zeyar Tun, the chargé d'affaires of Myanmar's military-controlled embassy in London. He was among the diplomats from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) hosted by Baroness Winterton, the minister responsible for the Indo-Pacific.
Two days later, Win Zeyar Tun attended another meeting with Lord Sonny Leong, the British minister responsible for small business and enterprise, to discuss trade-related issues with Asean diplomats.
Photographs from both meetings were subsequently published by Myanmar's military-controlled foreign ministry.
"International attention has been on US engagement with the Burmese military, but at the same time the British government appears to be quietly normalising relations with the Burmese military regime," said Minn Tent Bo, advocacy officer at Burma Campaign UK.
"There is clearly a policy shift happening from the British government, but they seem unwilling or unable to publicly justify why they are softening their approach to the Burmese military."
The campaign said it handed “another propaganda opportunity” to the military as its leader seeks to end years of international isolation.
While British officials had previously participated in meetings involving Myanmar representatives under Asean arrangements, ministerial-level meetings in government buildings accompanied by publicly released photographs marked a significant departure from the government's earlier approach.
Myanmar's foreign ministry confirmed both meetings in statements published on 19 and 20 October.
According to the ministry, Win Zeyar Tun also called on Britain to reconsider visa restrictions affecting Myanmar students seeking to study in the UK.
The second meeting focused on cooperation between small businesses, investment opportunities and educational partnerships between Britain and Asean countries, it said.
"Inviting a representative of the Burmese military regime to meetings at government departments and being pictured with them is not critical engagement, it is normalisation and acceptance of the military regime," said Minn Tent Bo.
"The British government keep saying it stands with the people of Burma, but they ignore our calls for new sanctions and instead are literally standing with representatives of the Burmese military."
The foreign office, however, denied that the UK’s position and engagement with Myanmar had changed.
“We continue to urge all parties to protect civilians and call on the military regime to end airstrikes against civilians, allow unhindered humanitarian access, and release all those arbitrarily detained, including Aung San Suu Kyi,” it told The Independent.
Soon after the 2021 coup, the British government issued a string of sanctions, including travel bans and asset freezes on three key figures in the military regime in response to human rights violations.
The government noted “serious human rights violations” by the military regime as the reason of sanctions.
However, no new sanctions have been passed against the military by the British government in almost two years despite escalating human rights violations.
This is despite a deteriorating humanitarian situation in Myanmar, where most of the legitimate and democratically elected leaders are in jail, freedom of the press is curtailed, and both junta and rebel forces have carried out regular strikes on schools, hospitals, and places of worship.
According to the United Nations, almost 20 million people – a third of the population – are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. At least 4 million people are internally displaced. Civil society organisations on the ground – who have more access to the conflict areas than the UN – put the figure much higher, perhaps at five million.

articles.full_text:
Perikatan Nasional can now contest next month’s Melaka election under its own name and symbol, after securing a temporary legal reprieve from deregistration.
SINGAPORE: Malaysia’s opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional (PN) on Thursday (Oct 22) secured a temporary legal reprieve from deregistration, clearing an immediate hurdle just nine days before nomination day for Melaka's state election.
But analysts say the court victory may do little to resolve the more fundamental problem of a deepening internal rift within PN, which could ultimately determine whether the coalition has a political future.
PN’s key component parties Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) have increasingly operated separately, including during the recent state elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
The Malaysian High Court on Thursday stayed PN's suspension and deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), allowing the coalition to resume political activities while it pursues a judicial review.
The decision comes a month before Melaka goes to the polls on Nov 14 and means PN can contest under its own name and symbol.
“For PN’s long-term future, it takes more than this stay. What’s the point of PN surviving in name but continuing to bicker?” said political scientist Syaza Shukri of the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM).
The question has become more pressing as PAS develops closer ties with the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), potentially leaving former prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin’s Bersatu increasingly isolated.
In Melaka, Barisan Nasional (BN), which is led by UMNO, and PAS have already agreed on a seat-sharing arrangement to contest the state election - the latest sign that Malaysia’s political alliances are shifting ahead of the next general election.
WHAT DID THE COURT DECIDE?
In granting the stay, Justice Azizan Md Arshad said “extraordinary circumstances” warranted the decision, citing the potentially irreversible consequences for PN’s participation in state elections, reported local news outlet The Star.
The stay will remain in effect pending the outcome of PN’s judicial review challenging RoS’s actions. The court has yet to decide whether the suspension and deregistration were lawful.
The RoS cancelled PN’s registration on Tuesday following months of infighting between PAS and Bersatu.
Tensions had become increasingly visible since last December, when eight Perlis assemblymen, five of whom were from Bersatu, withdrew support for the state's PAS chief minister in a move widely seen as orchestrated by figures aligned with Bersatu president Muhyiddin.
The fallout deepened mistrust between PAS and Bersatu and ultimately preceded Muhyiddin’s resignation as PN chairman.
The dispute came to a head in August when Muhyiddin complained to the RoS that Bersatu had been excluded from a PN supreme council meeting the previous month, in violation of the coalition’s constitution.
The regulator subsequently issued PN a show-cause notice on Sep 22 and suspended its activities the following day. After reviewing PN’s response, the regulator cancelled the coalition’s registration on Oct 20, saying its explanation “failed to refute the grounds for the cancellation of registration”.
PN secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan had questioned the timing of the decision so close to the Melaka election and vowed to challenge it in court.
IMMEDIATE REPRIEVE FOR MELAKA POLLS
The High Court’s decision has temporarily lifted the threat of the PN losing its common electoral symbol ahead of the Melaka state election on Nov 14.
PN chairman Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who is also PAS vice-president, welcomed the ruling as a positive development in the coalition’s efforts to “defend its rights through legal channels”.
“All election machinery must now focus on the Melaka state polls … Strengthen preparations, enhance cooperation and present the best possible offer to the people. We will continue moving forward,” he said in a statement on Thursday.
Analyst Adib Zalkapli, managing director of Viewfinder Global Affairs, said losing PN’s “recognisable and popular electoral symbol” would have been a “setback” for its component parties, particularly given the coalition’s appeal among Malay-Muslim voters.
“The PN brand has been useful especially in the more multiracial west coast of the peninsula,” Adib told CNA.
Melaka is located on Peninsular Malaysia’s west coast, where the PN brand is stronger than that of PAS, according to Syaza of IIUM.
“This (court decision) is good for PAS and friends except Bersatu in Melaka because they can use PN’s logo,” she told CNA.
In the 2021 Melaka state polls, PN won two seats, both through Bersatu. PAS failed to win any of the seats it contested under the coalition banner.
University Malaya political analyst Awang Azman Awang Pawi said losing the common logo would have affected “campaign consistency, coordination of electoral machinery and the clarity of candidates' political identities, particularly among undecided voters”.
The court ruling however does not necessarily resolve questions over how PN’s component parties will coordinate their campaigns.
Bersatu and the other PN parties have increasingly gone their separate ways.
In August’s Negeri Sembilan election, Bersatu announced its candidates separately and contested under its own symbol, including against PN candidates in eight constituencies.
Bersatu failed to win any of the 24 seats it contested independently, while PN won seven.
PN’s other parties include Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan), Malaysian Indian People’s Party (MIPP) and more recently, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan). Wawasan is led by former Bersatu’s deputy president Hamzah Zainudin after he was sacked in June 2026 amid internal party infighting.
COULD PN’S DIVISIONS ACCELERATE UMNO-PAS COOPERATION?
The divisions within PN come as Barisan Nasional (BN) and PAS deepen their electoral cooperation.
BN, led by deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, is part of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s federal unity government alongside his Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition but ties have come under strain in recent months, with both sides contesting state elections separately.
Following weeks of speculation over a possible electoral pact, BN chairman Zahid said this week that his coalition would contest 21 of Melaka’s 28 seats while PAS and its allies would field candidates in the remaining seven, reported Malay Mail.
BN would use its own logo while PAS and its PN allies would decide which symbol to contest under, he added.
The agreement between the two Malay-based parties follows cooperation in two other state elections.
During the Johor election in July, PAS instructed its supporters to back BN’s candidates in constituencies where PN was not contesting.
The cooperation deepened during the Negeri Sembilan polls in August, when BN fielded candidates in 25 seats and PN contested the remaining 11. Bersatu had contested separately.
Should PN ultimately lose its registration ahead of next general election, analysts say PAS could gain even greater freedom to pursue closer ties with UMNO, while Bersatu could find itself in a weaker political position.
Syaza of IIUM described Bersatu as a “thorn” in the relationship between UMNO and PAS.
Awang similarly said that PAS would have “greater room to determine its political direction” as Bersatu faces the risk of losing bargaining power if it no longer has access to PAS’ organisational support and voter networks during seat negotiations.
Adib of Viewfinder Global Affairs said that BN, and UMNO in particular, could emerge as the “biggest beneficiary” if PN were to lose its formal electoral platform.
“Without PN, UMNO through the BN coalition has a stronger case in seat negotiation process with PAS and Wawasan (of PN) as BN is obviously the stronger brand compared to (both parties) in the west coast,” Adib told CNA.
“It could weaken the opposition’s ability to mount a coordinated challenge against BN,” echoed Awang of UM.
Beyond the potential political realignments ahead of Malaysia’s next general election, analysts also questioned whether PN's legal reprieve would be enough to secure its long-term political future.
"Even if PN makes it sound like they want to challenge the deregistration, they still haven't come up with an acceptable solution about the impasse with Bersatu," said Syaza.
Awang similarly said that restoring PN's registration would not necessarily resolve disputes over leadership, power-sharing and trust among its component parties.
Syaza suggested that the remaining component parties could instead pursue a "looser arrangement", allowing them to coordinate seat allocations without being weighed down by their partners' political baggage.
Awang said the developments reflected the fragility of political coalition structures and the growing flexibility of political alliances in Malaysia.
"Malaysian politics is moving towards more fluid and pragmatic alliances driven by electoral interests rather than permanent coalition loyalties," he added.
Despite PN's legal troubles and internal divisions, Awang stressed that voters had not necessarily abandoned the opposition.
"What has been affected is the structure of political coordination, not necessarily the underlying base of public support," he said.
The changing political landscape came ahead of several key elections. Besides Melaka, Sarawak’s state assembly is expected to be dissolved soon.
Malaysia’s 16th general election must be held by February 2028, although Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has said he is open to considering calls for an earlier vote.

articles.title: Vice Chairman of Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee: Making Lotte Eco Smart City a new symbol of Thu Thiem. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Vice Chairman of Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee: Making Lotte Eco Smart City a new symbol of Thu Thiem.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh pledged to work alongside investors, creating the most favorable conditions to ensure the Lotte Eco Smart City Thu Thiem project is implemented comprehensively, with quality, safety, and efficiency.
On the morning of October 23rd, the Lotte Eco Smart City Thu Thiem project in functional zone 2A (Thu Thiem New Urban Area, An Khanh ward, Ho Chi Minh City) officially commenced construction with a total investment of approximately 60,000 billion VND (equivalent to 1.43 billion USD).
A "bright spot" in the goal of attracting $19 billion in FDI.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Vice Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Nguyen Cong Vinh emphasized that Ho Chi Minh City aims to build itself into a civilized and modern urban center, maintaining its role as the leading economic engine and a financial, commercial, and service hub for the region. In this strategic direction, the Thu Thiem New Urban Area plays a pivotal role in promoting high-quality growth.
According to the leaders of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee, in the context of increasingly fierce competition to attract international investment, Ho Chi Minh City prioritizes high-quality FDI flows, focusing on finance, technology, digital transformation , green economy, and sustainable development. Ho Chi Minh City plans to attract $19 billion in foreign investment in 2026, and the $1.43 billion project in Thu Thiem is a key highlight.
Ho Chi Minh City leaders also pledged that the local government would always stand alongside and create the most favorable conditions within the framework of the law to ensure the project is implemented comprehensively, safely, and effectively.
"With the city's development potential and the determination of the government at all levels, and the support of the domestic and international business community, I am confident that the Lotte Eco Smart City project will be successfully implemented, becoming a new symbol of the Thu Thiem new urban area, contributing to enhancing the attractiveness, competitiveness, and international standing of the city," said Nguyen Cong Vinh, Vice Chairman of the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City.
You may also like
Removing obstacles for the 7.45-hectare "mega-project"
Located adjacent to the Thu Thiem central square and lake, with direct views of the Saigon River and the existing city center, the Lotte Eco Smart City Thu Thiem project covers a total area of 74,513.4 m² (approximately 7.45 hectares) across 6 land plots. This is considered one of the most prime locations in the Thu Thiem central core.
The project is a large-scale, multi-functional urban complex, integrating Grade A office towers, commercial and retail podiums, services, accommodation, housing, and public spaces within a unified ecosystem, adhering to international standards for urban planning, development, and operation.
However, the journey to the groundbreaking ceremony was not entirely smooth. The project faced numerous challenges and fluctuations stemming from the international macroeconomic landscape and the COVID-19 pandemic, which prolonged the preparation process.
Commenting on this milestone, Mr. Jung Jung Tae, Consul General of South Korea in Ho Chi Minh City, said that the investor's perseverance and the Ho Chi Minh City government's determination to resolve legal difficulties and obstacles were key factors in helping the project overcome the barriers.
In particular, the realization of the joint venture model between Lotte Group and its domestic partner, Phat Dat Real Estate Development Joint Stock Company (PDR), has created an important foundation for the project to officially commence construction.
This model combines the financial capacity and international operational experience of a South Korean conglomerate with the market understanding and legal enforcement capabilities of a Vietnamese enterprise. Specifically, Phat Dat owns 35% of the charter capital of Lotte Properties HCMC Co., Ltd. and directly undertakes the development of commercial, service, office, and residential buildings.

Transforming vision into a tangible project.
According to the master plan, Lotte Eco Smart City Thu Thiem is being developed into a multi-functional complex encompassing finance, commerce, services, Grade A offices, and residential areas. The project boasts a prime location with excellent multi-modal transportation infrastructure, situated right next to the To Huu metro station and Ba Son bridge, directly connected to the Thu Thiem tunnel, and within the reach of key metro lines.
Representing the Vietnamese development partner, Mr. Bui Quang Anh Vu, General Director of Phat Dat Real Estate Development Joint Stock Company, stated that they always prioritize resources to translate into progress, commitments into quality, and vision into tangible projects. The project is oriented towards applying smart city solutions and green development standards (Eco Smart), from energy-optimized design and pedestrian-prioritized public spaces to digital technology- based management and operation.

Reportedly, the project has a total investment of up to 60,000 billion VND, and is located within...   Functional zone 2A, Thu Thiem New Urban Area, now located in An Khanh ward, Ho Chi Minh City. 
|  | 
| The Lotte Eco Smart City project has an investment capital of 60,000 billion VND. | 
 Spanning an area of 74,513.4 m² (approximately 7.45 hectares), the project comprises six adjacent land plots numbered 2-1 to 2-6. It is being developed as a large-scale, multi-functional urban complex, integrating Grade A office towers, commercial and retail spaces, services, accommodation, housing, and public spaces within a unified ecosystem, adhering to international standards for urban planning, development, and operation.  
 The project is a joint venture between Lotte Group and Phat Dat Real Estate Development Joint Stock Company, comprising three Lotte Group companies (Lotte Shopping Co., Ltd; Hotel Lotte Co., Ltd; Lotte Engineering & Construction Co., Ltd) and Phat Dat Real Estate Development Joint Stock Company. The project is developed by Lotte Properties HCMC Co., Ltd.
 Specifically, Phat Dat owns 35% of the charter capital of Lotte Properties HCMC Co., Ltd., according to Decision 4102/QD-UBND dated July 3, 2026, of the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City.
 This collaboration also involves the two companies allocating resources within the project development structure. Specifically, the housing component (blocks 2-2, 2-4, and 2-6) will be jointly developed by Phat Dat and Lotte.
 For the commercial-service and office component (blocks 2-1 and 2-3), Phat Dat is responsible for developing both high-rise blocks 2-1 and 2-3, along with the podium comprising 4 commercial-service floors and basement levels, with a total gross floor area (GFA) of approximately 219,722 m².
 Commercial component (blocks 2-5): Lotte is responsible for developing the entire high-rise section, along with the podium comprising 4 floors of commercial and service space and the basement levels.
 The project is being supported by three banking partners: Military Commercial Bank, Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade, and Vietnam Investment and Development Bank . 
|  | 
| The project includes components such as hotels, residential buildings, shopping malls, and financial centers. | 
 The project is of particular significance in promoting the formation of the new Thu Thiem urban center.
 This is also a large-scale FDI project, demonstrating the long-term confidence of international investors in the investment attractiveness and position of Ho Chi Minh City, while deepening the Vietnam- Korea cooperation relationship.
 For Phat Dat, becoming a direct co-development partner in one of the largest urban projects in the Thu Thiem core area demonstrates a strategy of focusing resources on high-value assets in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, while also providing an opportunity to collaborate with international partners to create an iconic project worthy of Thu Thiem, Ho Chi Minh City, and Vietnam's development aspirations.
 Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Mr. Nguyen Cong Vinh, Vice Chairman of the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City, stated that the project will not only create a smart, modern, and environmentally friendly urban complex but also contribute to perfecting the architectural appearance of the city center, improving the quality of life for residents, and increasing the city's attractiveness to global investors.
 “The City government highly appreciates Lotte Group’s long-term, serious, and responsible investment decision in Ho Chi Minh City. The presence and success of Korean businesses over the years have made a positive contribution to the socio -economic development of the city, while also deepening the comprehensive strategic partnership between Vietnam and Korea, opening up new and broader cooperation opportunities in many fields. Ho Chi Minh City always considers the Korean business community as one of its top priority partners,” Mr. Vinh said.
 According to Mr. Vinh, in the context of increasingly fierce competition to attract international investment, Ho Chi Minh City prioritizes high-quality FDI flows, focusing on the following sectors: finance, technology, digital transformation , green economy, sustainable development, and innovation. The city is determined to achieve the goal of attracting $19 billion in foreign investment in 2026, with this project, worth approximately $1.43 billion, being a clear example and a very important contribution to the city's FDI attraction results.
 Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Mr. Bui Quang Anh Vu, General Director of Phat Dat Real Estate Development Joint Stock Company, said that the company expects the success of Lotte Eco Smart City Thu Thiem to contribute to creating another landmark for Thu Thiem, enhancing the investment attractiveness of Ho Chi Minh City, deepening economic cooperation between Vietnam and South Korea, and contributing to Vietnam's modernization and integration process.
 "In a period when the city and the country are entering a new era of development, Phat Dat wishes not to stand aside from that journey, but, with its capabilities, to directly participate in creating new values for the city and the country," Mr. Vu said.
 Mr. Jung Sung Ho, General Director of Lotte Properties HCMC, stated that Lotte Eco Smart City aims to connect high-end offices, shopping malls, hotels, and luxury apartments into a single integrated urban ecosystem. By creating an environment where global businesses and talent converge, innovate, and create value, we are committed to contributing to the development of Ho Chi Minh City, aiming to build the city into a highly competitive international metropolis.
 “In the housing segment, we will also set a new standard. Lotte will mobilize all its accumulated capabilities in development, construction, distribution, and services to combine high quality with convenient infrastructure. Beyond simply providing housing, we will bring a safe and prosperous lifestyle, contributing to elevating the urban landscape and the quality of life for its residents. At the same time, throughout the entire project implementation process, Lotte will be responsible for the progress, quality, and safety to complete a space that city residents can be proud of for a long time,” said Mr. Jung Sung Ho.

Singapore’s rise as a science and technology powerhouse owes much to a national commitment to relentless innovation.
And for decades, the key institution fuelling the nation’s ambition is the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), established in 1991. From chip-fabrication breakthroughs to vaccine manufacturing and next-generation aviation technology, A*STAR has spent decades turning lab research into economic muscle.

articles.title: Maersk, Hateco Sign Vietnam Rail Freight Project Deal - Supply Chain Brain
articles.summary: Maersk, Hateco Sign Vietnam Rail Freight Project Deal  Supply Chain Brain
articles.full_text:
A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S, the world’s second largest container carrier, signed an agreement with Vietnamese conglomerate Hateco to develop a railway freight terminal network in Vietnam during President To Lam’s official visit to Denmark.
APM Terminals, the port operating unit of A.P. Moller-Maersk, inked a memorandum of understanding with Hateco in Copenhagen on October 27 to develop a container terminal system, according to a statement from Hateco. The deal takes the total estimated investment in supply chain infrastructure projects in Vietnam by the companies to $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion.
The proposed network, which will include a rail freight terminal in Haiphong and three container facilities across northern provinces, “aims to connect industrial parks, logistics hubs and production zones with major transport hubs,” it said.
President Lam also met other business leaders in the Danish capital, including executives from Lego Group, Carlsberg and Pandora, as Vietnam seeks to attract more investment, technology and expertise, according to the government website. Lam will then travel to Brussels for talks with European Union officials expected to cover trade, energy and education.
The container project comes as Vietnam ramps up infrastructure investment to support its multiyear double-digit economic growth target, seeking to boost spending to attract private capital and spur development. The Southeast Asian nation is pouring billions of dollars into upgrading its transport and logistics networks, with railways seen as a key priority.
Maersk has already partnered with Hateco on a $400 million container port project in Haiphong, according to the Vietnamese company. The Danish shipping giant is also expanding its investment in some joint projects, including the Lien Chieu container terminal port in Danang.
The planned rail freight facilities, which will use digital technology to enhance cargo handling and storage while connecting to seaports and rail infrastructure, are expected to ease road congestion and expand options for cross-border shipments, according to the statement.

articles.summary: Drugs worth RM16.2mil seized from unregistered house of worship in Klang  Free Malaysia TodayHoly smoke: Massive ganja and heroin haul found in Klang house of worship  Malay MailEight nabbed, drugs worth RM16mil seized in Selangor raids  The StarIllegal temple in Klang used to store drugs  The VibesPolice Seize RM16.2 Million Worth Of Drugs In Selangor Raids  SAYS
articles.full_text:
Selangor police chief Shazeli Kahar said the operation came to light after the arrest of a man who worked part-time at the premises, Berita Harian reported.
He said the house of worship was among four locations raided by the state police narcotics crime investigation department in five separate operations between Oct 13 and 19. The raids targeted four different syndicates.
In total, police seized 129 packets of suspected compressed cannabis buds weighing 81.3kg, 327 packets of compressed cannabis weighing 37kg, 3,510 ketamine liquid cartridges, 40kg of ketamine, 84 bottles of liquid ecstasy, 20.6kg of heroin and another 25.4kg of ketamine.
Police also seized assets worth RM54,835 from four local suspects, including a Honda Accord and a Proton Saga, Shazli added.
“We believe the cases involve drug syndicates. However, we are still verifying whether gangsterism or secret societies were also involved,” he was quoted as saying at a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters today.
Shazeli said eight people, comprising six men and two women aged between 19 and 48, were arrested to assist investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Those arrested included three foreign men and a woman who are believed to be linked to local and international drug syndicates, he said, adding that they had entered Malaysia on social visit passes.
“Some of the foreign suspects arrived just a day before their arrest, while others arrived a few days earlier.
“They are believed to have transited through KLIA before travelling to their next destinations, but we managed to detect drugs in their luggage,” he said.
Shazeli said the drugs were believed to have originated from a neighbouring country and were intended for distribution in Malaysia and overseas.
He said checks showed that only one suspect had a criminal record of seven drug-related and other criminal offences.
